context.summary: Found while drafting the T-claude-adapter brief against the Claude Code docs: background sessions are supervised by Claude Code itself and can be resumed with a new prompt, while holding a stream-json stdin open needs a daemon Ekumen does not have in v0.1. Permission mode stays Claude Code's default; bypassing permissions is never used.

options.tradeoff: No Ekumen daemon; the lead can `claude attach` to answer permission prompts; delivery to a busy or waiting session is queued until it is idle.
Immediate delivery, but needs a long-lived holder process per session that a one-pass CLI doesn't have, and nobody can answer permission prompts.

data.question: D-decision-delivery chose delivery on a managed session's input stream (a stream-json process Ekumen holds open). The T-claude-adapter brief instead starts managed sessions as Claude Code background sessions and delivers by resuming them. Adopt background sessions instead?
data.title: Deliver to managed sessions as Claude Code background sessions
